guide.summary: Pipedrive uses standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow on oauth.pipedrive.com, with 60-minute access tokens and refresh tokens that expire after 60 days of non-use. You register apps in the Developer Hub, which you reach through a developer sandbox account. Saving a draft with just a name and callback URL gives you a client_id and client_secret right away. Your biggest decision comes first. A private app skips review and can be shared with any Pipedrive company through a direct install link. A public app must pass a review that can take up to 21 business days, needs a demo video and test accounts, and stays unlisted until you click Publish. App type cannot be changed after creation. Composio has no managed auth for Pipedrive, so you need your own app.
auth_alternatives: Private app (OAuth, not listed): choose this to skip the Marketplace review and share the app through a direct install link with any Pipedrive company. The trade-off is that it is never listed in the Marketplace, and app type cannot be switched to public later.

Personal API tokens: only workable for your own single-account scripts. Pipedrive recommends OAuth instead, checks that approved apps do not collect users' API tokens, and on the Lite plan gives API tokens 20 requests per 2 seconds versus 80 for OAuth apps.

reasons_to_bring_own: Composio does not offer managed auth for Pipedrive, so you must supply your own client_id and client_secret.
Pipedrive requires OAuth 2.0 for Marketplace apps and does not allow approved apps to collect users' API tokens, so OAuth through your own app is the supported path.
OAuth apps get higher burst rate limits than API tokens on the Lite plan (80 versus 20 requests per 2 seconds).
build_or_borrow.verdict: Build your own Pipedrive OAuth app, because Composio has no managed auth for Pipedrive. Start as a private app shared by direct install link unless you need a Marketplace listing, since Pipedrive itself recommends OAuth over personal API tokens and private apps skip review.

prerequisites.text: A Pipedrive developer sandbox account, which is how you reach the Developer Hub (Settings > (company name) Developer Hub).
An app name and a working OAuth callback URL. These are the only fields needed to save a draft and get credentials.
For public apps: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages.
For public apps: a demo video explaining how each permission and scope is used and showing key functionality, plus working test accounts for reviewers.
A minimal scope list chosen in the OAuth & access scopes tab.

oauth.token_lifetime: Access tokens last 60 minutes. Refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use, and each use resets that to 60 days. Authorization codes expire in 5 minutes.
redirect_uri_rules: redirect_uri must match the callback URL registered with the app, or no code is sent.
The callback URL must actually work before you submit for approval.

blockers.text: App type (public or private) is permanent once chosen in Developer Hub.
blockers.workaround: Decide before creating the app. Pick private if you only need direct-link installs. Pick public only if you need a Marketplace listing and can accept review.

blockers.text: Public apps need review that can take up to 21 business days. Any rejection reasons arrive by email and must be fixed before you resubmit.
blockers.workaround: Use a private app with a direct install link while the public app is under review, or skip public listing entirely.

blockers.text: Review requires a demo video covering scope usage and working test accounts.
blockers.workaround: Record the video against the minimal scope set and prepare test accounts before clicking Send to review.

app_specific_gotchas.text: Public vs private app type cannot be changed after you create the app.
An approved app is unlisted by default. Nothing appears in the Marketplace until you click Publish in Developer Hub.
Refresh tokens die after 60 days without use. Users of an agent that stays idle that long will have to reconnect unless you refresh on a schedule.
Users must accept all requested scopes at once, and the admin scope only works if the installing user is a company admin.
API usage is capped by a daily per-company token budget based on plan and seats. Once it is exhausted, requests return HTTP 429.

limits: A private app needs no approval. Any Pipedrive company can install it through the direct install link, but it is never listed in the Marketplace.
The claims do not say whether a public app's draft can be installed by outside companies before approval. Do not rely on it.
Admin-scoped apps can only be installed by users with admin rights in the company.

Rate limits apply to every app: a daily token budget per company of 30,000 base tokens times a plan multiplier times seats, plus purchased top-ups. Requests beyond it return HTTP 429. On the Lite plan, OAuth apps get 80 requests per 2 seconds, compared with 20 for API tokens.
Access tokens last 60 minutes. Refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use, so idle installs must re-authorize.
unapproved_mode.breaks_at: It breaks the moment you want a Marketplace listing. App type is immutable, so a private app cannot be converted. You must register a new public app, which goes through review (up to 21 business days) and then needs a manual Publish. What happens to existing installs during that switch is not documented.

steps.title: Get a developer sandbox account
steps.detail_md: Sign up for a Pipedrive developer sandbox account. It is the only way into the Developer Hub, and you need it before any app work or approval process starts.

steps.title: Open the Developer Hub
steps.detail_md: In the sandbox account go to **Settings > (company name) Developer Hub**. Older docs call it Marketplace Manager. The probe confirms developers.pipedrive.com is reachable.

steps.title: Decide: public or private app (irreversible)
steps.detail_md:
App type cannot be changed after you choose it. The agent can lay out the trade-off, but you make the call.

- **Private**: no review and no Marketplace listing. You share it through an unlisted direct install link, and any Pipedrive company can install it.
- **Public**: must pass Marketplace approval. Reviews can take up to 21 business days. After approval you can list it publicly.

My recommendation: if your agent's users can be onboarded with a link, start private and ship now. Choose public only if you need a Marketplace listing.

steps.title: Prepare callback URL and minimal scope list
steps.detail_md:
The agent drafts these two things:

- **Callback URL**: the exact URL your backend will serve. The code is only sent to a `redirect_uri` that matches the registered callback, so it must be live and correct.
- **Scope list**: the fewest scopes your use case needs. Users must accept or deny all scopes together. Avoid the admin scope unless you truly need it, because it requires the installing user to have admin rights in their company.

The provided material lists no individual scope names, so map them from the OAuth & access scopes tab.

steps.title: Save a draft app to get client credentials
steps.detail_md: Create the app in Developer Hub. A draft only needs an app name and the OAuth callback URL. Saving the draft gives you the `client_id` and `client_secret`. The other required fields are only checked when you submit for review. Store the secret securely.

steps.title: Set scopes
steps.detail_md: In the **OAuth & access scopes** tab, select only the scopes from step 4.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth 2.0 flow
steps.detail_md:
Pipedrive publishes no discovery document: both well-known URLs return 404. Hardcode the endpoints.

- **Authorize**: `GET https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/authorize` with `client_id`, `redirect_uri` and `state`.
- **Token**: `POST https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/token`, authenticated with HTTP Basic Auth using client_id:client_secret. Putting them in the body works but is not recommended.
- Exchange the code right away, because it expires in 5 minutes.
- Access tokens last 60 minutes. Refresh them through the same token endpoint.
- Refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use, and each use resets that clock. Plan for re-auth when a user goes idle for a long time.
- Never collect users' API tokens. Approved apps must use OAuth as their primary auth method.

steps.title: Handle rate limits and the daily budget
steps.detail_md: Each company gets a daily token budget of 30,000 base tokens x plan multiplier x seats, plus any top-ups. Once that budget is used up, requests return HTTP 429. Add backoff and surface the error clearly to users. OAuth apps get a higher burst limit than API tokens on Lite: 80 versus 20 requests per 2 seconds.

steps.title: Install and test end to end
steps.detail_md: Install the app on your sandbox. The user sees a consent dialog listing the scopes and clicks **Allow and install**. No separate workspace-admin approval step is documented. Confirm that the callback works, tokens arrive and refresh succeeds. A broken callback blocks submission.

steps.title: Private path: share the install link (done)
steps.detail_md: If you chose private, share the direct installation link with your users. There is no review and no wait, and you are finished here. Skip the remaining steps.

steps.title: Public path: draft Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
steps.detail_md: Both pages are required. The agent can draft the text. You review it and publish it on your domain.

steps.title: Public path: record demo video and set up test accounts
steps.detail_md: Record a video that explains why you use each permission and scope and shows the app's key functionality. Also prepare working test accounts for the reviewers.

steps.title: Public path: complete the form, preview, Send to review
steps.detail_md: Fill in the full registration form, install and test, preview the listing, then click **Send to review**.

steps.title: Public path: Pipedrive review
steps.detail_md: Pipedrive owns this time. The documented upper bound is **up to 21 business days**. The minute figure is only 21 x 24h, so actual calendar time is longer once weekends are counted. No typical duration is documented.

steps.title: Public path: fix rejection reasons if any
steps.detail_md: Rejection reasons arrive by email. Fix all of them before you resubmit. Each resubmission goes back into review, and no shorter re-review time is documented.

steps.title: Public path: click Publish
steps.detail_md: An approved app stays unpublished and unlisted until you click **Publish** in Developer Hub.

belief_diff.topic: Does letting arbitrary users connect require provider review or verification?
belief_diff.prior_belief: Yes, Pipedrive requires the app to pass a Marketplace review before arbitrary users outside your own company can install and connect it.
belief_diff.finding: Public apps must pass Pipedrive's approval process before listing, while private apps skip review and are shared via an unlisted direct install link; the claims do not explicitly say unapproved public apps are limited to the developer's own company.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Pipedrive Marketplace app review typically takes about 10 business days.
belief_diff.finding: The claims state public app review may take up to 21 business days, not about 10.

belief_diff.topic: Limits while the app is unapproved
belief_diff.prior_belief: While unapproved, the app can only be installed by users in the developer's own company account, capped at 1 company and no external installs.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not address installation limits or company caps for unapproved apps.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Listing and submitting a public Pipedrive Marketplace app is free, with no fee charged to the developer.
belief_diff.finding: The claims do not mention any fees or costs for listing or submitting an app.

belief_diff.topic: Key prerequisites (domain, privacy policy, video, business verification)
belief_diff.prior_belief: A verified developer account, a privacy policy URL, a demo video, and a support contact are required, while a company domain is needed and business verification is not required.
belief_diff.finding: The claims require a developer sandbox account (not a verified one), a demo video, and both a Terms of Service and a Privacy Policy page; they do not mention a support contact, company domain, or business verification.

belief_diff.prior_belief: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS and exactly match a pre-registered value in the app settings, with no wildcards allowed.
belief_diff.finding: The claims say the redirect_uri must match the registered callback URL and a non-functioning callback must be fixed before submission, but say nothing about HTTPS or wildcard rules.
